title: What if you never slept again?

vo.text: What if you never slept again? Not tired. Just... never.
vo.tts: What if you never slept again? Not tired. Just... never.

vo.text: Night one. You feel incredible. Eight free hours. You learn guitar. You clean everything.
Night three. Your brain is a browser with 400 tabs open. Your hands don't feel like yours.
Night eleven. The record is 11 days. After that, nobody knows — because nobody has made it further.
vo.tts: [whispers] Night eleven. The record is 11 days. After that, nobody knows — because nobody has made it further.

vo.text: But here's the thing. Sleep isn't rest. It's a wash cycle.
Every night, your brain shrinks by a fifth and flushes out the waste it made all day. Skip it, and the waste stays.
Which means the version of you that never sleeps isn't a superhero. It's a room nobody cleans.
So... what if you never slept again? You'd finally understand why you do.

beats.visual: Blocky character in bed, eyes snap open; moon hangs above; fully composed at frame 0
Character sprints through night chores; clock spins; confetti
Browser tabs stack up on its head; hands float off slightly
Calendar flips to day 11; a question mark where day 12 should be
Cut to black; a washing machine door opens on the brain
Brain shrinks 20%, waste particles flush; then a cluttered room fills with trash
Back to the bed; eyes close; final frame matches frame 0 with eyes shut
